mechanism: CapLite does not ask the agent's model to write a security policy. It derives the policy from the tool schemas, commits the planned write calls before any tool output is read, and admits a write only if every argument that decides the recipient, amount, object or destination appears in the user's own request. Injected text in tool results therefore cannot add a write or redirect one. It is evaluated on AgentDojo with 15 small open-weight models.
claim: No attack succeeds in 13,935 attacked AgentDojo episodes, with utility under attack of 29.0% against CaMeL's 27.2% at 18% of its tokens.
why_not_testable: Reproducing it needs model answers from open-weight models and AgentDojo runs, and there is no local LLM here.
needs: A local or hosted open-weight model.
one_line: A prompt-injection defence that lets a write happen only when every recipient and amount is stated in the user's own request, with no model-written policy.
idea_why: Checking write arguments against the user's own words is a simple, auditable rule that does not rely on the model behaving.
breakdown: Read the paper and its code if released. The idea can be copied cheaply into any Proteus agent that sends or posts: list the write tools, mark which arguments decide the target, and refuse a call unless those values appear in the original task text. A later night could run it against AgentDojo once a model is available. No hired work is needed beyond a security reviewer if it protected real money.
